scenes.headline: See the whole picture.
scenes.subtitle: Threat Surface Area Assessment Tool
scenes.body: TSAAT brings recorded cyber terrain evidence into a clearer view.

scenes.headline: From records to context.
scenes.subtitle: Devices. Software. Vulnerabilities. Links.
scenes.body: Explore recorded devices, installed software, vulnerability observations and their relationships.

scenes.headline: Two views. One terrain.
scenes.subtitle: Governance + Discovery
scenes.body: Use Governance for summaries and Discovery to examine the records behind them.

scenes.headline: Evidence for better questions.
scenes.subtitle: Understand. Investigate. Communicate.
scenes.body: Use the evidence to ask better questions, investigate gaps and explain what you find.

scenes.subtitle: The foundation
scenes.body: OPORD/01-2019 starts CMDB and dynamic discovery. An enterprise platform reaches DPE and DSE by June 2022.

scenes.headline: Q3 2022
scenes.subtitle: Make the connections
scenes.body: Configuration Management processes are established, including ICT System Modelling.

scenes.subtitle: Assess the critical systems
scenes.body: DSR: HICTO orders 66 and 67 assess about 87 critical ICT Systems against 28 compliance questions. TSAAT v1.0 reports the findings.

scenes.subtitle: Scale the inventory
scenes.body: DIIS captures ICT System inventory and ownership. OMWOW models about 3,000 systems. TSAAT v2.0 and training arrive in Q4 2025.

scenes.headline: Q1 2026
scenes.subtitle: A wider conversation
scenes.body: TSAAT is presented to DSOC and Cyber Command as a reporting tool for visibility of the Cyber Terrain.

scenes.headline: Jan 2027
scenes.subtitle: The next chapter - planned
scenes.body: TSAAT v3.0 is designed in Q4 2026 for DSOC needs, with delivery planned for January 2027.

terrain.label: More than a list of devices

scenes.headline: More than a device list.
scenes.subtitle: The environment your organisation relies on
scenes.body: Cyber Terrain includes the devices, software, networks and services you look after.

scenes.headline: Layers that work together.
scenes.subtitle: Devices + software + networks
scenes.body: A device runs software. Networks connect devices. Together, they support ICT Systems and services.

scenes.headline: Relationships add meaning.
scenes.subtitle: The connections matter
scenes.body: Recorded relationships help explain how technical components fit together.

scenes.headline: Know the shape of it.
scenes.subtitle: Keep the evidence in view
scenes.body: Understand what is recorded, how it connects and where the picture is incomplete.

scenes.headline: Choose your view.
scenes.subtitle: Start with the question
scenes.body: Select the cyber terrain and snapshot you need before interpreting a result.

scenes.headline: Find the pattern.
scenes.subtitle: Governance
scenes.body: Read summaries to see recorded patterns, missing details and discovery gaps.

scenes.headline: Follow the evidence.
scenes.subtitle: Discovery
scenes.body: Explore the underlying records, open details and follow recorded relationships.

scenes.headline: Explain what you found.
scenes.subtitle: A shared basis for discussion
scenes.body: Use reports and exports to support a focused conversation about the evidence.

scenes.headline: A system has a purpose.
scenes.subtitle: More than a single component
scenes.body: An ICT System brings components together to deliver an intended function.

scenes.headline: Networks make connections.
scenes.subtitle: The paths between components
scenes.body: Networks link devices and help components exchange information.

scenes.headline: Different views. Related evidence.
scenes.subtitle: System, network and component
scenes.body: A system view explains purpose and ownership. A network view explains connectivity.

scenes.headline: Follow the recorded links.
scenes.subtitle: An illustrative system
scenes.body: Use recorded relationships to explore how components, networks and ICT Systems fit together.

scenes.headline: A finding is a starting point.
scenes.subtitle: Security vulnerabilities
scenes.body: A vulnerability observation records a potential weakness associated with a device or software.

scenes.headline: Add the context.
scenes.subtitle: Which device? Which software?
scenes.body: Examine the affected records, recorded CVE details and the source that reported the observation.

scenes.headline: Separate signal from proof.
scenes.subtitle: Observation is not exploitation
scenes.body: A recorded finding is not proof that a weakness is exploitable or has been exploited.

scenes.headline: Investigate. Then prioritise.
scenes.subtitle: Evidence supports judgement
scenes.body: Combine recorded evidence with system context and validation to inform the next step.

scenes.headline: What is missing?
scenes.subtitle: Shadow IT
scenes.body: An unfamiliar address or device can reveal a gap between observed activity and known inventory.

scenes.headline: Keep the roles separate.
scenes.subtitle: Observed device + reporting device
scenes.body: Distinguish the unknown device from the known device that reported seeing it.

scenes.headline: Unknown does not mean hostile.
scenes.subtitle: A lead to investigate
scenes.body: An unexplained record could reflect an inventory gap, an expected device or something requiring attention.

scenes.headline: Investigate the gap.
scenes.subtitle: Identify. Validate. Follow up.
scenes.body: Review the evidence and establish the device identity, owner and place in the terrain.

scenes.headline: Start with the service.
scenes.subtitle: What needs to keep working?
scenes.body: Services depend on ICT Systems, networks, software and devices working together.

scenes.headline: Trace the dependencies.
scenes.subtitle: An illustrative dependency path
scenes.body: Follow recorded relationships to identify components that may support a service.

scenes.headline: Ask what else could be affected.
scenes.subtitle: Potential impact, not a prediction
scenes.body: A component issue may have wider implications. Recorded links help frame the investigation.

scenes.headline: Validate with the owners.
scenes.subtitle: Turn a connection into a conversation
scenes.body: Confirm dependencies and operational context with owners before drawing conclusions about service impact.

reporting.label: A focused answer. Context you can share.

scenes.headline: Start with your view.
scenes.subtitle: A question gives the evidence purpose
scenes.body: Start with the information available in your TSAAT view and the question you need to answer.

scenes.headline: Narrow the view.
scenes.subtitle: Terrain. Snapshot. Relevant filters.
scenes.body: Select cyber terrain and date, then check the loaded snapshot. Use relevant Discovery search and table filters.

scenes.headline: A focused answer.
scenes.subtitle: Governance summaries / Discovery records
scenes.body: Use Governance for scoped summaries and Discovery to inspect matching records. Choose the view that answers your question.

scenes.headline: Report with context.
scenes.subtitle: Keep scope and snapshot with the result
scenes.body: Governance PDFs use header scope and snapshot. Explorer Excel exports matching filtered rows. Check what the download includes before sharing.

benefits.label: A clearer picture. A better conversation.

scenes.headline: See what you have.
scenes.subtitle: Visibility
scenes.body: Bring recorded inventory, relationships and observations into a view people can explore.

scenes.headline: Find the questions.
scenes.subtitle: Investigation
scenes.body: Spot missing details and follow the evidence behind summaries and findings.

scenes.headline: Share the understanding.
scenes.subtitle: Communication
scenes.body: Use consistent views, reports and exports to discuss the same evidence.

scenes.headline: Know the terrain. Take the next step.
scenes.subtitle: Explore the TSAAT Feature Guide
scenes.body: Choose a feature, learn how it works and practise using the guide.
